findings.reason: isUnknownOption (lib/yargs-parser.ts:972-989) returns !hasFlagsMatching(...), and every pattern it checks starts with ^-+. So 'file.js' counts as unknown, and the branch at line 225 calls pushPositional, which pre-empts the halt-at-non-option break at line 397. Both reviewers traced the same input and got the same wrong result.
findings.claim: Removing the /^-/ guard makes every plain positional an 'unknown option' when unknown-options-as-args is on. The positional is pushed to argv._, so halt-at-non-option never stops parsing.
findings.evidence: The line now reads `if (arg !== '--' && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg)) { pushPositional(arg)` with no `continue`. `isUnknownOption` (line 972) returns `!hasFlagsMatching(...)`, and every pattern it checks starts with `^-+`. A value like `./file.js` therefore matches none of them, so the function returns true. That makes the first branch win before the `else if (configuration['halt-at-non-option']) { notFlags = args.slice(i); break }` branch at line 397 is reached. For example, `['./file.js', '--foo']` with both settings on now produces `foo: true` instead of `_: ['./file.js', '--foo']`.
